The report before you today presents a recommended approach for the allocation of the 2025 city owned land incentives. These incentives are proposed to support the construction of 256 new affordable housing units.
This is the second package of development incentives utilizing funding from the housing accelerator fund.

As a reminder, in May of 2024, committee approved an incentive report outlining the proposed incentive programs being offered using approximately $35 million in funding from the housing accelerator fund to boost housing supply.
The capital grants detailed within the support were previously approved through that May incentive report.
Of the $35 million, approximately $15 million has been set aside for this round of city owned land development incentives.
To support a gain in the total number of new affordable rental units available to low income households with incomes below this is Saskatchewan household income maximums.
This funding stream focuses on the areas of highest need along Saskatoon's current housing continuum.
A call for proposals was open for just under three months between September 23rd, 2024 and December 13th, 2024.
Applicants proposing construction of new affordable rental units on city owned land were eligible to apply for capital grants of up to $50,000 per unit and a five year incremental tax abatement.
Approved projects are also eligible for a building and development permit fee rebate of up to $1,500 per unit upon issuance of the final building permit.
Eight applications were received for three city owned sites and were evaluated and scored based on weighted categories with criteria.
Three applications are being brought forward today for consideration for incentives.
So as mentioned in total, there are 256 new affordable rental units being recommended to receive the development incentives through this report.
And administration is recommending three projects receive a five year incremental tax abatement.
In addition to recommending an exception to the innovative housing policy to wave all off site levies for the development to be located at 1635.
Priority for funding has been given to registered nonprofits housing cooperatives indigenous organizations and our governments and first nations.
Appendix one of the report provides greater detail for each of the allocated capital grants and proposed tax abatements that administration is recommending today.
In terms of tax abatements in accordance with the city's act, tax abatements are subject to city council approval based on information from the corporate financial services division.
If the three eligible projects are approved, the city will for go and estimated total of approximately $1.2 million of municipal and library tax revenue over the five years.

The bill is provided on page three of the report that shows an overview of the estimated incremental tax abatements and the final abatements will be based on the actual assessed value determined upon final inspection of the completed projects.

As the estimated education property tax for the proposed developments located at 231 23rd Street East 155 3rd Avenue North and a portion of 1635.
We'll exceed the 25,000 per tax year if approved by city council applications requesting provincial approval of this exemption will be submitted.

For over 43 years, Swads has been championing the integration and settlement of newcomers and refugees into the Saskatoon community.

Through its extensive programming and community partnerships, Swads has continued to work to build a welcoming and inclusive Saskatoon, where all individuals regardless of their background can thrive.
This mission aligns with the need to address the city's growing demand for affordable housing and community services, particularly for the vulnerable populations.

Recognizing these challenges, Swads is embarking on a transformative initiative to create a affordable housing community, a purpose-built centralized facility that integrates affordable housing with comprehensive community services.

Located in Saskatoon's downtown core, the development aims to become a hub of opportunity, empowerment and connection for newcomers, racialized groups, indigenous peoples, seniors, youth and individuals living with disabilities.
The facility presents a bold vision to provide stable, affordable and accessible housing to low-income individuals and families with the focus on newcomers and racialized groups.
We aim to deliver wraparound services that support settlement, education, employment and community engagement, tailored to cultural and linguistic needs.
We aim to foster an inclusive environment that promotes intergenerational and cross-cultural interactions, emphasizing culturally responsible design and programming.

And formed by the principles of equity, sustainability and inclusivity, this project is designed to address systemic barriers to housing and services, while contributing to the city's broader goals of creating a vibrant and sustainable downtown.
We know Saskatoon faces a growing demand for affordable and accessible housing, particularly among vulnerable populations.
The city of Saskatoon's housing needs assessment highlights that 18% of households are between 15,000 and 45,000 annually, categorizing them as low income.
While 4.33% are less than 15,900 annually, placing them in a very low income bracket, according to the city of Saskatoon's 2023 housing needs assessment report.
The city has experienced a significant population search, largely driven by international immigration.
Between October 2022 and October 2023, Saskatoon's population grew by 14,400 individuals, the largest year over year increase in the post-war era, with 85% of that growth attributed to newcomers.
This trend underscores the critical lead for affordable housing options, located near essential services, public transit and employment hubs.
The breakdown for the proposed housing development unit includes 30, 2 bedroom units, 23 bedroom units and 10, 4 bedroom units all in the family oriented units category.
We aim to build 20 studio units and 10, 1 bedroom units for single resident units.
We aim to build 5, 1 bedroom and 5, 2 bedroom units under the accessible units category.
And 5, 2 bedroom units, 5, 3 bedroom units and 2, 4 bedroom units for the temporary housing units category.
The total units to be built will be 112 units.
These configurations align with the needs of the target demographics, including low income families, newcomers, racialized groups and individuals requiring accessible accommodations.

Outside of the residential units, the welcome place will offer a holistic approach to community that will include community spaces, educational and training facilities, daycare services, administrative offices, retail and commercial areas that would include potential doctor offices, financial institutions and an ethnic grocery store.
And then green and outdoor spaces will be included.
In conclusion, the welcome place affordable housing community represents a transformative and forward thinking response to Saskatoon's housing and community service needs.
Design to address systemic barriers and prioritize inclusivity.
The project integrates affordable housing with wraparound services and a vibrant and sustainable and strategically located facility.
Innovative design, strong operational framework work and a dedicated team of partners.
Welcome place is prepared to make a lasting impact.
By providing safe, accessible and affordable housing alongside essential support services.
This development will empower residents, strengthen community ties and enhance the economic and social fabric of Saskatoon.
As a vital community hub, it will not only meet the immediate needs of newcomers and racialized groups, but will also contribute to downtown Saskatoon's revitalization plan.
As well as the long term vibrancy and resilience of the community as a whole.
Together, we can build a stronger, more inclusive Saskatoon for generations to come.
